grades: Entering 10th to 12th grade in the fall of the program year (2026 page)
name: Woodland Park Zoo Teen Ambassador Volunteer Program
what_you_do: Weekly cohort meetings on conservation careers, public speaking and teamwork, plus 20 self-scheduled volunteer shifts at the zoo, including Zoomazium, new habitats and animal behavior observation.
who_can_apply: High school students entering grades 10 to 12. No prior experience required. The teen page does not state a minimum age; 15 teen volunteers were taken in 2026.
pay_detail: Active teen volunteers receive a $300 summer stipend to help with transportation, lunches and shoes. No participation fee is listed.
duration: June to September: orientation day, at least 7 of 10 Wednesday meetings (3:30 to 6:30 pm), 20 volunteer hours between June 29 and Sept 6 (2026 dates)
deadline_text: 2026 cohort: application deadline Friday, March 27, 2026, 5:00 pm; Q&A sessions in March; interviews mid-April; decisions early May. 2027 dates are not posted.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application by the deadline. Email teenambassadors@zoo.org for help. Sign up for recruitment updates at zoo.org/volunteer.
notes: The zoo's general volunteer program has its own rules (at least 16, one-year commitment, applications opening January 2027); those do not appear on the teen page. Applicants who identify with autism or ADHD can get application and interview support from Canopy Neurodiversity Foundation. Marked work permit unknown because of the stipend.
